For a signed quantity use\n    ``diverging``; when the gap between two values is the story use\n    ``dumbbell``; past ~20 categories ``lollipop`` stays cleaner.\n    \"\"\"\n    series = _series(spec)\n    n = max(len(s.get(\"values\") or []) for s in series)\n    cats = _labels(spec, n)\n    y = np.arange(n)\n    height = 0.8 / len(series)\n    for i, s in enumerate(series):\n        vals = _numbers(s.get(\"values\"), f\"series[{i}].values\", expect=n)\n        errs = s.get(\"errors\")\n        offset = (i - (len(series) - 1) / 2) * height\n        ax.barh(\n            y + offset,\n            vals,\n            height * 0.92,\n            label=literal(s.get(\"label\")) if s.get(\"label\") else None,\n            color=PALETTE[i % len(PALETTE)],\n            xerr=_error_bars\n/ai-inventor/.claude/skills/aii-data-fig-gen/scripts/chart_renderers_cluster.py\n\ndef _import_scipy_hierarchy():\n    \"\"\"The real collaborator: scipy's clustering module. Its own function so a\n    test can inject a fake that raises ``ImportError`` without reaching for\n    scipy itself or patching ``builtins.__import__``.\"\"\"\n    from scipy.cluster import hierarchy\n\n    return hierarchy\n\n\ndef _hierarchy(*, import_hierarchy=_import_scipy_hierarchy):\n    \"\"\"scipy's clustering module, or a message saying it is missing.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        hierarchy = import_hierarchy()\n    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - present wherever sklearn is\n        raise SpecError(\n            \"hierarchical clustering needs scipy, which is not importable here \"\n            f\"({exc}). It ships with scikit-learn, which this pipeline depends \"\n            \"on — install it, or use 'heatmap', which needs no clustering.\"\n        ) from exc\n    return hierarchy\n\n\ndef _matrix_of(spec: dict, key: str = \"matrix\") -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"The observations, as a rectangular float array, or a message.\"\"\"\n    raw = spec.get(key)\n    if not isinstance(raw, list) or not raw or not all(isinstance(row, list) for row in raw):\n        raise SpecError(f\"'{key}' must be a non-empty list of equal-length rows of numbers\")\n    widths = {len(row) for row in raw}\n    if len(widths) != 1:\n        raise SpecError(\n            f\"'{key}' rows have differing lengths {sorted(widths)}. 'average' is the safe default and \"\n            \"'ward' the usual choice when the features are on one scale.\"\n        )\n    return method\n\n\ndef _names_for(spec: dict, key: str, count: int, what: str) -> list[str]:\n    raw = spec.get(key)\n    if not raw:\n        return [str(i + 1) for i in range(count)]\n    if not isinstance(raw, list):\n        raise SpecError(f\"'{key}' must be a list, got {type_name(raw)}\")\n    if len(raw) != count:\n        raise SpecError(\n            f\"'{key}' has {len(raw)} entries but there are {count} {what}. \"\n            \"A name attached to the wrong row is worse than no name at all, so \"\n            \"this is refused rather than padded.\"\n        )\n    return [literal(name) for name in raw]\n\n\ndef _linkage(matrix: np.ndarray, method: str, what: str):\n    if matrix.shape[0] < 2:\n        raise SpecError(\n            f\"clustering needs at least two {what}, got {matrix.shape[0]}. \"\n            \"One observation has nothing to be close to.\"\n        )\n    if matrix.shape[0] > _MAX_LEAVES:\n        raise SpecError(\n            f\"{matrix.shape[0]} {what} is past what a readable tree carries \"\n            f\"(max {_MAX_LEAVES}) — the leaves come out thinner than their own \"\n            \"labels. For two values per category use {instead}.\"\n        )\n    return series[0]\n\n\ndef _two_series(spec: dict, kind: str, instead: str) -> tuple[dict, dict]:\n    \"\"\"The before/after pair these two-column charts take.\"\"\"\n    series = _series(spec)\n    if len(series) != 2:\n        raise SpecError(\n            f\"'series' has {len(series)} entries but a {kind} compares exactly two — \"\n            f\"series[0] is the first value and series[1] the second. {instead}\"\n        )\n    return series[0], series[1]\n\n\ndef _num(value: float, fmt: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"A formatted number carrying a real minus sign, not a hyphen.\n\n    ``format(-8.4, \"+.1f\")`` produces U+002D, while the house style sets\n    ``axes.unicode_minus`` so every TICK on the same figure uses U+2212. Left\n    alone, a waterfall printed \"−5\" on its axis and \"-5.7\" on the bar right\n    next to it: two different glyph widths for the same sign, which a reader\n    registers as a rendering fault even without naming it.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = format(float(value), fmt)\n    return \"−\" + text[1:] if text.startswith(\"-\") else text\n\n\ndef _sort_order(spec: dict, values: np.ndarray, *, default: str) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Row order for a ranked chart. Stable, so ties keep the author's order.\"\"\"\n    how = spec.get(\"sort\", default)\n    if how in (None, False, \"none\"):\n        return np.arange(values.size)\n    if how is True or how == \"desc\":\n        return np.argsort(-values, kind=\"stable\")\n    if how == \"asc\":\n        return np.argsort(values, kind=\"stable\")\n    raise SpecError(f'\\'sort\\' must be \"desc\", \"asc\" or \"none\", got {how!r}')\n\n\ndef _nice_ceiling(value: float) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Round an auto-chosen upper bound up to a number a reader can hold.\n\n    Scaling a radar to ``max × 1.05`` is correct and unreadable: it put the\n    rings at 22.05 / 44.1 / 66.15 / 88.2. Rounding UP to a 1/2/2.5/5 × 10ⁿ\n    step keeps every point inside the outer ring — nothing is cropped, which\n    is the part that would matter — while giving round ring labels. An\n    explicit ``rlim`` is never touched.\n    \"\"\"\n    if value <= 0:\n        return 1.0\n    scale = 10.0 ** math.floor(math.log10(value))\n    for step in (1.0, 2.0, 2.5, 5.0):\n        if value <= step * scale * (1.0 + 1e-12):\n            return step * scale\n    return 10.0 * scale\n\n\ndef _text_width_in(chars: int, points: float) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Rough width in inches of ``chars`` characters set at ``points``.\"\"\"\n    return chars * points * _EM_RATIO / 72.0\n\n\ndef _axes_size_in(ax) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Pre-draw estimate of THIS axes' box in inches, width and height.\n\n    Sizing a label reserve off the FIGURE is right exactly once — when the\n    figure holds one axes. Inside a ``panel`` grid the same renderer gets a\n    third of the width, and a reserve computed from the whole figure is three\n    times too small: the slope chart's end-labels went straight through the\n    y-axis ticks of the panel beside it.\n\n    ``get_position()`` is the subplot's share of the figure BEFORE\n    constrained layout runs, so it reads 0.775 for a lone axes and 0.23 for a\n    3-column cell — the distinction that matters. Layout then reclaims the\n    margins and hands back roughly 15% more, hence the correction; it stays\n    deliberately on the low side, becaus\n/ai-inventor/.claude/skills/aii-data-fig-gen/scripts/chart_renderers_dist.py\n\ndef _positive_int(spec: dict, key: str, default: int, *, maximum: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"An integer spec key that becomes an allocation or a label count.\"\"\"\n    value = spec.get(key, default)\n    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 1:\n        raise SpecError(f\"'{key}' must be a positive integer, got {value!r}\")\n    if value > maximum:\n        raise SpecError(\n            f\"'{key}' of {value} is past what a figure can show legibly (max {maximum})\"\n        )\n    return value\n\n\ndef _grouped(spec: dict) -> tuple[list[np.ndarray], list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Per-group samples and their labels — the shape of a group-wise chart.\n\n    An EMPTY group is rejected rather than skipped. Skipping renumbers every\n    row after it, so the label \"Ours\" ends up against the samples belonging\n    to the next group along and the figure is wrong in a way no reader can\n    see.\n    \"\"\"\n    series = _series(spec)\n    data = []\n    for i, s in enumerate(series):\n        values = _numbers(s.get(\"values\"), f\"series[{i}].values\")\n        data.append(values)\n    labels = [literal(s.get(\"label\") or str(i + 1)) for i, s in enumerate(series)]\n    return data, labels\n\n\ndef _xy_of(series_entry: dict, index: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n    \"\"\"The ``x``/``values`` pair of one series, both gated and length-matched.\"\"\"\n    raw_y = series_entry.get(\"values\") or series_entry.get(\"y\")\n    if not raw_y or not series_entry.get(\"x\"):\n        raise SpecError(f\"series[{index}] needs both 'x' and 'values'\")\n    y = _numbers(raw_y, f\"series[{index}].values\")\n    x = _numbers(series_entry.get(\"x\"), f\"series[{index}].x\", expect=y.size)\n    return x, y\n\n\ndef _axis_fraction(value: float, axis: np.ndarray, *, log: bool) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Where ``value`` sits along ``axis`` — 0 at the low end, 1 at the high.\n\n    Measured in the axis's OWN scale. On a log axis a fixed fraction of the\n    linear range is a sliver at one end and most of the plot at the other, so\n    a margin expressed linearly is no margin at all exactly where it matters.\n    \"\"\"\n    low, high = float(axis.min()), float(axis.max())\n    if log and low > 0:\n        low, high, value = (float(np.log10(v)) for v in (low, high, max(value, 1e-300)))\n    return (value - low) / (high - low) if high > low else 0.5\n\n\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# distributions\n# --------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef render_ridgeline(ax, spec: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Stacked density curves, one row per group, overlapping slightly.\n\n    Each group's distribution is drawn as a filled Gaussian-KDE curve on its\n    own baseline, with the rows spaced closer than the curves are tall so a\n    tall neighbour rises into the row above. Every row shares one x-axis, so\n    a shifted mode or a second bump is read off directly.\n\n    Choose it over ``violin`` or ``box`` once there are more than about six\n    groups. A violin grid spends the figure's WIDTH on one strip per group\n    and runs out of it; a ridgeline spends the page's height, which is free,\n    and stays readable at twenty rows. Choose ``violin``/``box`` instead when\n    the groups are few and the quartiles are the finding, ``ecdf`` when the\n    comparison is about tails or a threshold, and ``strip`` when n per group\n    is small — a density curve drawn through eight points implies a\n    smoothness the data does not support.\n\n    Rows are normalised to their own peak, so they compare SHAPE rather than\n    frequency. Put n in the group's label when it varies between groups.\n\n    Keys: ``series[].values``, ``series[].label``, ``overlap`` (0 = rows just\n    touch, default 0.7), ``bandwidth`` (override Silverman's rule),\n    ``medians`` (mark each row's median).\n    \"\"\"\n    data, labels = _grouped(spec)\n    overlap = _scalar(spec.get(\"overlap\", 0.7), \"overlap\")\n    if not 0.0 <= overlap <= 3.0:\n        raise SpecError(\n            f\"'overlap' is {overlap:g}; it must be between 0 a\n/ai-inventor/.claude/skills/aii-data-fig-gen/scripts/chart_renderers_extra.py\n\ndef render_step(ax, spec: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A piecewise-constant series — the value holds, then jumps.\n\n    For anything that changes at discrete moments and is CONSTANT between\n    them: a learning-rate schedule, a batch-size ramp, a policy or config\n    that switched at a known step. Choose over ``line``, which draws a\n    sloped segment between points and so implies the value passed through\n    every intermediate level — for a schedule that is simply false, and a\n    reader will take the slope literally. ``where`` may be ``post`` (the\n    default, value holds forward from each x), ``pre`` (it holds backward\n    into each x), or ``mid`` (it changes halfway between them).\n\n    ``markers`` puts a dot at each actual sample, which separates the measured\n    points from the held value between them.\n    \"\"\"\n    series = series_of(spec)\n    where = spec.get(\"where\", \"post\")\n    if where not in (\"post\", \"pre\", \"mid\"):\n        raise SpecError(f\"'where' must be post, pre or mid, got {where!r}\")\n    # Read BEFORE the loop: the axis was switched to log after every series had\n    # been drawn, so nothing was in a position to refuse a zero. `line`,\n    # `scatter`, `scaling` and `pareto` all call `require_positive` and `step`\n    # did not — measured, a step series containing 0.0 with `logy: true` drew\n    # at exit 0 with matplotlib masking the point, which is the exact silent\n    # data loss SKILL.md says this check exists to stop.\n    log_y = flag(spec, \"logy\")\n    for i, s in enumerate(series):\n        y = numbers(s.get(\"values\"), f\"series[{i}].values\")\n        if log_y:\n            require_positive(y, f\"series[{i}].values\", \"y\")\n        raw_x = s.get(\"x\") or spec.get(\"x\")\n        x = numbers(raw_x, f\"series[{i}].x\", expect=y.size) if raw_x else np.arange(y.size)\n        style = series_style(i)\n        label = literal(s[\"label\"]) if s.get(\"label\") else None\n        ax.step(x, y, where=where, label=label, **style)\n        if flag(spec, \"markers\"):\n            ax.plot(x, y, \"o\", color=style[\"color\"], markersize=4)\n    if log_y:\n        ax.set_yscale(\"log\")\n    draw_legend(ax, spec, series)\n\n\ndef render_hist2d(ax, spec: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A joint distribution of two variables as a binned density grid.\n\n    For the SHAPE of a relationship when there are enough points that a\n    scatter is a solid blob — correlation structure, ridges, multiple\n    clusters. Choose over ``scatter`` past roughly two thousand points, and\n    over ``hexbin`` when the axes are naturally rectangular (integer counts,\n    binned scores) so square cells align with the data rather than cutting\n    across it. Both axes are binned, so unlike a scatter no point can hide\n    another.\n\n    ``cmap`` overrides the sequential default; the rainbow family is refused,\n    because density is the only thing this figure encodes.\n    \"\"\"\n    series = series_of(spec)\n    s = series[0]\n    x = numbers(s.get(\"x\"), \"series[0].x\")\n    y = numbers(s.get(\"values\") or s.get(\"y\"), \"series[0].values\", expect=x.size)\n    bins = spec.get(\"bins\", 40)\n    # Only the minimum is checked here. The shared `bins` gate in chart_validate\n    # already refuses non-integers, bools and anything below 1, and it runs\n    # first — so a bool or a float never reaches this line, and 1 is the single\n    # value this adds. A 1x1 hist2d is one box holding every point, which is a\n    # colourbar and no information.\n    if bins < 2:\n        raise SpecError(f\"'bins' must be an integer of at least 2, got {bins!r}\")\n    *_, mesh = ax.hist2d(x, y, bins=bins, cmap=colour_map(spec, SEQUENTIAL_CMAP))\n    bar = ax.figure.colorbar(mesh, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, pad=0.03)\n    bar.set_label(literal(spec.get(\"cbar_label\", \"Count\")))\n\n\ndef render_residual(ax, spec: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Residuals against fitted values, with the zero line.\n\n    The standard regression diagnostic, and the figure that shows whether a\n    model's errors are structured. A healthy plot is a formless band around\n    zero; a funnel means the var\n/ai-inventor/.claude/skills/aii-data-fig-gen/scripts/chart_renderers_more.py\n\ndef render_beeswarm(ax, spec: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Every observation as a point, spread sideways in proportion to density.\n\n    For when the reader must see the raw sample AND its density — feature\n    attributions per instance, per-seed scores, latency per request. Choose\n    over ``strip``, which offsets points at random and so still overlaps at\n    any real n: the eye reads the resulting clumps as density and they are\n    partly collision. Choose over ``violin`` when n is small enough that a\n    smoothed density would invent shape the data does not support — twelve\n    seeds and twelve thousand look identical once smoothed.\n\n    Offsets are computed by binning on the value axis and spreading each\n    bin's members evenly across a width proportional to how many it holds, so\n    the outline traces the real histogram and the figure is reproducible\n    rather than differently-random each run. The width available is fixed, so\n    past roughly a hundred observations in one bin the markers do begin to\n    touch; at that n the sample is large enough that ``violin`` is the better\n    choice anyway, and its smoothing is no longer inventing anything.\n\n    ``point_spread`` (default 0.34) is how wide the swarm may get in category\n    units, and ``show_median`` (default true) draws the rule through each\n    group.\n    \"\"\"\n    series = series_of(spec)\n    width = number_option(spec, \"point_spread\", 0.34, minimum=0.0)\n    for i, entry in enumerate(series):\n        values = numbers(entry.get(\"values\"), f\"series[{i}].values\")\n        # Bin height of roughly one marker, so members of a bin are the points\n        # that would otherwise sit on top of each other.\n        span = float(values.max() - values.min()) or 1.0\n        bins = max(1, min(60, int(np.sqrt(values.size) * 3)))\n        index = np.clip(((values - values.min()) / span * bins).astype(int), 0, bins - 1)\n        offsets = np.zeros_like(values, dtype=float)\n        # Scale against the busiest bin in THIS series, so the widest point of\n        # the swarm is full width and every other is its share of that. The\n        # divisor used to be a constant 8, which meant any bin past 8 members\n        # drew at full width: 100 observations at one value and 8 at another\n        # came out exactly the same ±0.34, reporting a 12x density difference\n        # as no difference at all — in the one channel this chart type has.\n        busiest = max(int(np.bincount(index, minlength=bins).max()), 2)\n        for slot in range(bins):\n            members = np.where(index == slot)[0]\n            if members.size < 2:\n                continue\n            # Evenly spaced, centred: −w … +w with the widest bin at full width.\n            spread = np.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, members.size)\n            offsets[members] = spread * width * (members.size / busiest)\n        ax.scatter(\n            np.full(values.size, float(i)) + offsets,\n            values,\n            s=18,\n            alpha=0.75,\n            color=PALETTE[i % len(PALETTE)],\n            edgecolors=\"none\",\n        )\n        if flag(spec, \"show_median\", True):\n            median = float(np.median(values))\n            ax.plot(\n                [i - width * 1.3, i + width * 1.3],\n                [median, median],\n                color=\"#333333\",\n                linewidth=1.6,\n                solid_capstyle=\"butt\",\n            )\n    labels = labels_for(spec, len(series))\n    ax.set_xticks(np.arange(len(series)), labels=labels)\n    ax.set_xlim(-0.6, len(series) - 0.4)\n\n\ndef render_volcano(ax, spec: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Effect size against significance, with both thresholds drawn.\n\n    The screen figure for many comparisons at once — every ablation, every\n    feature, every prompt variant on one panel — where the finding is which\n    ones are BOTH large and significant. Choose over a ``bar`` of effect\n    sizes, which cannot show whether a difference survived multiple-testing\n    correction, and over a table of p-values, which cannot show whether the\n    si\n/ai-inventor/.claude/skills/aii-data-fig-gen/scripts/chart_renderers_sets.py\n\ndef _positive_int(spec: dict, key: str, default: int | None, *, maximum: int) -> int | None:\n    \"\"\"An integer spec key that becomes a count of things drawn.\"\"\"\n    value = spec.get(key, default)\n    if value is None:\n        return None\n    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value < 1:\n        raise SpecError(f\"'{key}' must be a positive integer, got {value!r}\")\n    if value > maximum:\n        raise SpecError(f\"'{key}' of {value} is past what a figure can show (max {maximum})\")\n    return value\n\n\ndef _axes_inches(ax, spec: dict) -> tuple[float, float]:\n    \"\"\"Roughly how big this Axes will be, in inches, before layout runs.\n\n    Needed because two charts here decide what FITS — a rectangle's label, a\n    column of set names — and a fit test has to be in the same units as the\n    thing being fitted. The figure's size is known exactly; the axes' share of\n    it is not, because constrained layout only settles at draw time.\n\n    ``get_position`` reports the pre-layout box, which the default subplot\n    margins shrink to about 77% of its slot in each direction; constrained\n    layout hands nearly all of that back to an axes carrying no ticks or\n    labels. Normalising by those margins turns the pre-layout box into an\n    estimate of the final one, and it stays proportionally right inside a\n    ``panel``, where the slot is genuinely half the figure.\n\n    The TITLE has to be subtracted here rather than left to layout, because\n    the caller sets it AFTER the renderer returns — so no measurement taken\n    inside a renderer can see it. {"stdout": "=== README.md head ===\n# Causal depth × site grid: where does Qwen3-4B's refusal live?\n\nThis is an intervention study on three checkpoints of the same model:\n\n- `Qwen/Qwen3-4B`, called **instruct** here;\n- `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-SafeRL`, the official safety fine-tune, called **SafeRL**;\n- `mlabonne/Qwen3-4B-abliterated`, a community uncensored checkpoint, called **abliterated**.\n\nIt asks three questions:\n\n- **Where** in depth and **where** in the token stream does the request-harmfulness direction do causal work on refusal and over-refusal?\n- Does that differ between instruct and SafeRL?\n- Do the cheap readouts built on that direction move when behaviour moves?\n\nIt is the first *executed* site-local causal grid of this research run. The iteration-3 plan for this grid was never executed.\n\n> RESULTS: see [Results](#results). Every number there is regenerated by `src/analyze.py` from the checkpointed cells into\n> `results/analysis.json`, `results/summary_tables.md` and `method_out.json`.\n\n**Headline findings**\n\n- **The request axis F causally controls the *form* of the first response token, not the refusal decision.** Projecting F out at the last prompt position in B4-B6 is CAUSAL (registered F1 rule) for the first-token refusal-onset mass. At P and in the teacher-forced windows it is *matched displacement*, h ← h − c_F·u, where c_F is the coefficient the F row of the same item removes in the same pass, so the R/F displacement ratio is exactly 1. At D′/E it is the plan's own-coefficient form h ← h − (h·F)u. u is a unit Gaussian direction orthogonalised to span{F, N6}. cat > render_fig_specificity.py <<'PY'
"""Render fig_specificity from fig_specificity_spec.json.

Hand-written because no catalogue type carries four marker-coded classes,
per-cell multiplicity and a reference band at once. House style, layout
passes and legibility gates from the aii-data-fig-gen skill are applied so
the figure belongs to the same set as the generated ones.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import warnings
from collections import defaultdict
from pathlib import Path

SKILL = Path("/ai-inventor/.claude/skills/aii-data-fig-gen/scripts")
sys.path.insert(0, str(SKILL))

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt  # noqa: E402

from chart_geometry import assert_text_is_legible, fit_point_labels  # noqa: E402
from chart_style import (  # noqa: E402
    PALETTE,
    apply_house_style,
    assert_all_glyphs_rendered,
    assert_axis_names_are_unique,
    assert_layout_applied,
    assert_legends_clear_of_data,
    assert_series_are_distinguishable,
    clear_legends_of_data,
    figsize_for,
    fit_legends,
    fit_tick_labels,
    fit_titles,
    literal,
    place_legend,
    place_point_label,
)

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


def main() -> None:
    spec = json.loads((HERE / "fig_specificity_spec.json").read_text())
    classes = {c["key"]: c for c in spec["classes"]}
    dodge = dict(zip([c["key"] for c in spec["classes"]], spec["class_dodge"]))

    # One drawn marker per (class, false_alarms, sensitivity) cell; its area and
    # inset digit carry how many readouts sit there, so nothing is hidden and no
    # coordinate is moved off its measured value.
    cells: dict[tuple, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for r in spec["readouts"]:
        cells[(r["class"], r["false_alarms"], round(r["sensitivity"], 4))].append(r["name"])
    assert sum(len(v) for v in cells.values()) == 32, "lost a readout"

    apply_house_style()
    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as warned:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(
            figsize=figsize_for(spec["aspect"], spec["width_in"]), layout="constrained"
        )

        ax.axvline(
            spec["gap_line_x"],
            color="#BBBBBB",
            linestyle="--",
            linewidth=1.1,
            zorder=0,
        )

        for key, cls in classes.items():
            colour = PALETTE[cls["palette_index"]]
            xs, ys, sizes = [], [], []
            for (ckey, fa, sens), names in sorted(cells.items()):
                if ckey != key:
                    continue
                xs.append(fa + dodge[key])
                ys.append(sens)
                sizes.append(40 + 58 * (len(names) - 1))
            ax.scatter(
                xs,
                ys,
                s=sizes,
                marker=cls["marker"],
                color=colour,
                alpha=0.85,
                edgecolors="white",
                linewidths=0.6,
                label=literal(cls["label"]),
                zorder=3,
            )

        # Multiplicity digits, drawn inside the marker they belong to.
        for (ckey, fa, sens), names in sorted(cells.items()):
            if len(names) < 2:
                continue
            ax.text(
                fa + dodge[ckey],
                sens,
                str(len(names)),
                ha="center",
                va="center",
                fontsize=6.5 if len(names) < 4 else 8,
                color="white",
                fontweight="bold",
                zorder=4,
            )

        for lab in spec["point_labels"]:
            at = lab["at"]
            place_point_label(
                ax,
                literal(lab["text"]),
                (at["false_alarms"] + dodge[at["class"]], at["sensitivity"]),
                offset=tuple(lab["offset"]),
                fontsize=8,
            )

        ax.set_xlabel(literal(spec["xlabel"]))
        ax.set_ylabel(literal(spec["ylabel"]))
        ax.set_title(literal(spec["title"]))
        ax.set_xlim(*spec["xlim"])
        ax.set_ylim(*spec["ylim"])
        ax.set_xticks(spec["xticks"])
        ax.set_yticks(spec["yticks"])

        place_legend(ax, loc="lower right", framealpha=0.95)
        fit_legends(fig)
        clear_legends_of_data(fig)
        fit_tick_labels(fig)
        fit_titles(fig)
        clear_legends_of_data(fig)
        fit_point_labels(fig)

        assert_text_is_legible(fig)
        assert_legends_clear_of_data(fig)
        assert_series_are_distinguishable(fig)
        assert_axis_names_are_unique(fig)
        assert_layout_applied(list(warned), fig)
        assert_all_glyphs_rendered(list(warned))

    fig.savefig(HERE / "fig_specificity_v0.pdf")
    fig.savefig(HERE / "fig_specificity_v0.png", dpi=220)
    print(f"cells={len(cells)} readouts={sum(len(v) for v in cells.values())}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

{"stdout": "def fit_point_labels(fig) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Move a point's name off whatever it landed on, measured after layout.\n\n    A renderer picks the offset before the axes has its final size, so \"up and\n    to the right by five points\" can put a name straight through a neighbouring\n    marker, through a curve, or through another name. All three are invisible\n    to the renderer, and the first two are invisible to the text gate as well,\n    because neither a marker nor a line is text.\n\n    Each recorded label is tried at each position in turn and keeps the first\n    that is clear of the data and of every other painted label. If none is\n    clear the original is kept: a figure that says what the renderer meant, and\n    which the gate can then refuse on the evidence, beats one silently shuffled\n    somewhere no better.\n    \"\"\"\n    labels = getattr(fig, \"aii_point_labels\", [])\n    if not labels:\n        return\n    fig.canvas.draw()\n    renderer = fig.canvas.get_renderer()\n    painted = {id(ax): _drawn_data(ax) for ax, _ in labels}\n    ours = {id(annotation) for _, annotation in labels}\n    skip = _undrawn_tick_labels(fig)\n    # Everything already on the page that a name must not land on. Collected\n    # once: it does not change while the labels move, and re-walking the figure\n    # for every label at every corner turned a 60-point volcano into minutes.\n    fixed: list[list[tuple[float, float]]] = []\n    for artist in fig.findobj(matplotlib.text.Text):\n        if id(artist) in ours or id(artist) in skip:\n            continue\n        if not artist.get_visible() or not artist.get_text().strip():\n            continue\n        try:\n            fixed.append(_oriented_box(artist, renderer)[0])\n        except (RuntimeError, ValueError):\n            continue\n    import numpy as np\n\n    grids = {\n        key: (\n            np.asarray(points or [(np.inf, np.inf)], dtype=float),\n            np.asarray(radii if points else [0.0], dtype=float),\n        )\n        for key, (points, radii) in painted.items()\n    }\n    placed: list[list[tuple[float, float]]] = []\n    for ax, annotation in labels:\n        grid, radii = grids[id(ax)]\n        best, chosen = None, _LABEL_CORNERS[0]\n        for corner in _LABEL_CORNERS:\n            annotation.set_position(corner)\n            try:\n                quad, _ = _oriented_box(annotation, renderer, pad=_MARKER_CLEARANCE, trim=True)\n            except (RuntimeError, ValueError):\n                break\n            x0, y0, x1, y1 = _bounds(quad)\n            # Measure each marker against ITS OWN radius instead of inflating\n            # the box by the largest one on the axes.   `results/scores/pairs_long.json`

Two conventions in the source are easy to misread and are resolved in the spec:

- the source's `frac_noop_ci_covers_0` ("FA 14/15") is the count of no-op pairs
  **not** flagged. The false-alarm count plotted here is
  `15 − covers_0` = `len(false_alarm_pairs)`, recorded per readout.
- sensitivity denominators are **9 for most readouts and 8** for `N8`, `N9_*`,
  `AMS_T1`, `AMS_T2`, `greedy_refusal_rate` and `greedy_refusal_rate_onset`.

**Corrections applied to the draft's figure specification.** The draft gave
`N4_onset`, `N4_peak` and `N4_width` a sensitivity of 0. The artifact records
3/9, 1/9 and 1/9. The figure plots the artifact's values. The draft also
attributed 7/9 sensitivity to the activation family; 7/9 is `B7`, which is a
**weight** readout, and the caption says so.

**Flagged but plotted as recorded.** `AMS_T2_drift` (0/8) later failed
validation against the reproduced pair list, and `regex` / `regex_namefree`
were flagged unverifiable for a differently-named key. They are drawn as the
aggregate file records them and called out in the caption.

## Layout devices (neither moves a measured value)

- **Multiplicity.** 32 readouts fall into 23 distinct cells. One marker is
  drawn per cell; its area and its inset digit give how many readouts share it,
  so no readout is hidden under another.
- **Class dodge.** Markers are offset horizontally by at most 0.12 according to
  class, so that readouts of different classes landing on the same cell (only
  `N6_benign_sep` and `regex`, both at 0 false alarms and 5/9) stay visible.

## Layout

| path | what it is |
|---|---|
| `fig_specificity_spec.json` | the figure's source: all 32 readouts, provenance, labels, caption |
| `render_fig_specificity.py` | the renderer — reads the spec, writes the PDF and PNG |
| `fig_specificity_v0.pdf` | **the deliverable** (vector, Type-42 fonts) |
| `fig_specificity_v0.png` | raster copy, for reading the figure back |
| `.aii/manifest.yaml` | disposability decisions (none needed — see below) |

## How to run

```bash
python render_fig_specificity.py
```

Deterministic: the same spec gives the same PNG every time. Needs `matplotlib`
and `numpy` (both already in the pipeline image) and the house style from
`/ai-inventor/.claude/skills/aii-data-fig-gen/scripts`, which the renderer puts
on `sys.path` itself.

The figure is hand-written matplotlib rather than a `chart_gen.py` type: no
catalogue type carries four marker-coded classes, per-cell multiplicity and a
reference band at once. It still imports `apply_house_style`, `place_legend`,
`place_point_label` and the full fitter/assert chain
(`fit_legends` → `clear_legends_of_data` → `fit_tick_labels` → `fit_titles` →
`clear_legends_of_data` → `fit_point_labels`, then `assert_text_is_legible`,
`assert_legends_clear_of_data`, `assert_series_are_distinguishable`,
`assert_axis_names_are_unique`, `assert_layout_applied`,
`assert_all_glyphs_rendered`), so it matches the rest of the paper's figures.

To change a value, edit `fig_specificity_spec.json` and re-run — never edit the
renderer to move a point.

## Restoring removed files

Nothing in this workspace is marked for deletion. It contains only text, code
and two small rendered images, all of them deliverables a later step reads, and
nothing above the 10 MB auto-keep floor — so `.aii/manifest.yaml` has no
entries and there is nothing to restore. Should the figures be lost, re-render
them with `python render_fig_specificity.py`.
